title: Battle of Kapetron
description: A Seljuk raiding army under Ibrahim Inal fought a Byzantine and Georgian army at Kapetron, the first great clash between Turks and Byzantium on the Anatolian frontier.

title: Sultanate of Rum founded
description: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish, a Seljuk prince, sets up a sultanate on land taken from Byzantium after Manzikert, the beginning of lasting Turkish rule in Anatolia.

title: Siege of Nicaea
description: The First Crusade besieges the Seljuk capital, which surrenders to the Byzantines, and the sultans afterwards rule from Konya.

title: Battle of Dorylaeum
description: The army of the First Crusade defeated the Seljuks of Rum at Dorylaeum, opening the crusader march across Anatolia; the sultanate later recentered its capital at Iconium (Konya).

title: Battle of Myriokephalon
place: Pass of Tzivritze, east of Isparta (site not identified)
description: Kilij Arslan II ambushes Manuel I's army in a mountain pass on its march to Konya, ending Byzantine hopes of retaking central Anatolia.

title: Seljuks take Antalya
description: Kaykhusraw I takes the port of Antalya, giving the sultanate its first outlet to the Mediterranean.

title: Battle of Yassıçemen
description: Kayqubad I and his Ayyubid allies defeat the Khwarazmian ruler Jalal al-Din, the last strong power between Anatolia and the advancing Mongols.

title: Battle of Köse Dağ
place: Köse Dağ, between Sivas and Erzincan
description: A Mongol army under Baiju crushes Kaykhusraw II, and the Sultanate of Rum becomes a Mongol client state.

title: Death of Rumi
description: The Persian-language poet and mystic dies in Konya, where his tomb becomes the centre of the Mevlevi order of dervishes.

title: Osman founds the Ottoman state
description: Osman I, ruler of a small principality on the Byzantine frontier, becomes independent of the Seljuks; the date is traditional.

title: Capture of Bursa
description: After a long blockade the Ottomans take Bursa from the Byzantines and make it their first capital.

title: Battle of Kosovo
description: Murad I's army meets a Serbian-led coalition; both rulers die, and Serbia afterwards becomes an Ottoman vassal.

title: Battle of Ankara
description: Timur defeats and captures Sultan Bayezid I, and the Ottoman state falls into eleven years of civil war.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Mehmed II takes Constantinople after a 53-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire and giving the Ottomans their capital.

title: Battle of Chaldiran
description: Selim I defeats the Safavid shah Ismail I, fixing Ottoman control of eastern Anatolia.

title: Battle of Ridaniya
description: Selim I defeats the Mamluks outside Cairo, bringing Egypt, Syria and the holy cities of Arabia under Ottoman rule.

title: Battle of Mohács
description: Suleiman the Magnificent destroys the Hungarian army and King Louis II dies in the retreat, opening Hungary to partition.

title: First siege of Vienna
description: Suleiman's army fails to take Vienna, the furthest Ottoman advance into central Europe.

title: Battle of Lepanto
description: The fleet of the Holy League destroys most of the Ottoman fleet in the last great battle fought between galleys.

title: Battle of Vienna
description: A relief army under John III Sobieski breaks the second Ottoman siege of Vienna, after which the empire loses ground in Europe.

title: Treaty of Karlowitz
description: The Ottomans cede most of Hungary to the Habsburgs and land to Venice and Poland, their first large loss of territory by treaty.

title: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
description: Defeated by Russia, the Ottomans give up the Crimean Khanate and open the Black Sea to Russian ships.

title: Janissaries destroyed
description: Mahmud II puts down a Janissary mutiny and abolishes the corps, clearing the way for a modern army.

title: Edict of Gülhane
description: The edict promises security of life and property and equal treatment for all subjects, beginning the Tanzimat reforms.

title: First Ottoman constitution
description: Abdul Hamid II proclaims a constitution and a parliament, which he suspends in 1878.

title: Treaty of San Stefano
description: After defeat by Russia the Ottomans accept a large autonomous Bulgaria, which the Congress of Berlin cuts back later that year.

title: Young Turk Revolution
description: Faced with an army revolt in Macedonia, Abdul Hamid II restores the constitution of 1876.

title: Battle of Lule Burgas
description: The Bulgarians defeat the main Ottoman army in Thrace in the bloodiest battle of the First Balkan War and drive it back to the Çatalca line, 30 km from Constantinople.

title: Raid on the Sublime Porte
description: Unionist officers led by Enver and Talat storm the government offices and force out the grand vizier, who was ready to give up Edirne, opening the Committee of Union and Progress's rule.

title: Fall of Adrianople
description: After a siege of almost five months Bulgarian and Serbian troops take Edirne, the former Ottoman capital, deciding the First Balkan War.

title: Treaty of London
description: The peace ending the First Balkan War leaves the Ottoman Empire only a strip of Thrace east of a line from Enez to Midye, ending five centuries of rule over most of the Balkans.

title: Treaty of Constantinople
description: Bulgaria accepts the Ottoman recovery of Edirne, retaken in the Second Balkan War, fixing a border in Thrace close to Turkey's present one.

title: Ottomans retake Edirne
description: While Bulgaria was losing the Second Balkan War, Ottoman troops recovered Edirne without a battle after its Bulgarian garrison withdrew.

title: Black Sea raid
description: Ottoman warships under a German admiral shell Russian ports, bringing the empire into the First World War on the side of the Central Powers.

title: Armenian leaders arrested in Constantinople
description: Hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and community leaders are arrested and deported, the date by which the Armenian genocide is remembered.

title: Allied landings at Gallipoli
description: British and French forces land to open the Dardanelles; Ottoman defenders hold them until they withdraw in January 1916.

title: Armistice of Mudros
description: The Ottoman Empire leaves the First World War and opens the Straits to the Allies.

title: Allied occupation of Constantinople
description: Allied forces enter the capital two weeks after the armistice and occupy it formally in March 1920.

title: Greek landing at Smyrna
description: Greek troops land with Allied backing, starting the Greco-Turkish War.

title: Mustafa Kemal lands at Samsun
description: The conventional starting point of the Turkish national movement.

title: Treaty of Sèvres
description: The sultan's government signs a partition of the empire that is never ratified.

title: Battle of the Sakarya
description: The Greek advance on Ankara is stopped.

title: Battle of Dumlupınar
description: The Great Offensive breaks the Greek army in Anatolia.

title: Armistice of Mudanya
description: The Allies concede Eastern Thrace and Constantinople to the Ankara government.

title: Abolition of the sultanate
description: The Grand National Assembly ends the Ottoman monarchy after roughly six centuries.

title: Treaty of Lausanne
description: Replaces Sèvres and sets the borders of the new Turkish state.

title: Republic of Turkey proclaimed
description: The Grand National Assembly declares a republic, with Mustafa Kemal as its first president.

title: Caliphate abolished
description: The assembly abolishes the caliphate and sends the Ottoman dynasty into exile.

title: Sheikh Said rebellion
description: Kurdish and Zaza rebels led by Sheikh Said rise against the new secular republic; the revolt is crushed and Said is hanged.

title: Latin alphabet adopted
description: A law replaces the Arabic-based Ottoman script with a Latin alphabet for Turkish.

title: Dersim massacre
description: Army operations against a rising in Dersim, renamed Tunceli in 1935, kill thousands of Alevi Kurds and drive many more from the province.

title: Death of Atatürk
description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk dies after fifteen years as president, and İsmet İnönü succeeds him.

title: Turkey joins NATO
description: Turkey and Greece become members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

title: Military coup of 1960
description: Army officers overthrow the Democrat Party government; Prime Minister Adnan Menderes is hanged the next year.

title: Invasion of Cyprus
description: Turkish forces land in northern Cyprus after a coup backed by the Greek junta, and the island is left divided.

title: Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) founded
description: Kurdish students led by Abdullah Öcalan founded the Kurdistan Workers' Party at a village congress, committed to an independent Kurdish state.

title: Military coup of 1980
description: The armed forces take power after years of political violence and rule until 1983.

title: PKK insurgency begins
description: The Kurdistan Workers' Party attacks Eruh and Şemdinli, opening an insurgency in the southeast that kills some 40,000 people by 2012.

title: Öcalan captured
description: Turkish agents seize the PKK's leader Abdullah Öcalan in Kenya and fly him to İmralı island, where he is sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment.

title: İzmit earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake near the Sea of Marmara kills more than 17,000 people.

title: Coup attempt of 2016
description: A faction of the armed forces tries to seize power and fails within a day.

title: Constitutional referendum
description: Voters narrowly approve constitutional changes that abolish the office of prime minister and create an executive presidency.

title: Executive presidency takes effect
description: Erdoğan is re-elected in the first round of the presidential election and the new presidential system approved in 2017 comes into force.

title: Istanbul mayoral election rerun
description: After the electoral council annuls the opposition's narrow victory in March, Ekrem İmamoğlu wins the rerun for mayor of Istanbul by a wide margin.
